candidates.title: Shrinkflation paradox: scanner data says shoppers barely react; experiments say once they know, it feels like deception
candidates.publisher: Marketing Science (Evangelidis, ESADE) — author repository PDF
candidates.claim: Pre-registered experiments (>7,000 participants per ESADE summary): downsizing judged unfair more often than an economically equivalent price rise (e.g. chocolate 44.4% vs 30.7%; OJ 46% vs 26.7%). Study 4: low transparency 69.3% vs 53% unfair; with clear disclosure the gap vanishes (36.9% vs 35.4%). Mechanism: perceived deception, not money lost.
candidates.note: SELECTED (with C02 as counter-evidence, C03 as concrete case, C04 as current regulatory spark).

lenses.verification: Read author PDF directly for percentages; ESADE summary read for sample size and the 'honesty' quote. Janssen & Kasinger scanner paper confirmed via RePEc (abstract page); full INFORMS page blocked, so their numbers (1.92% downsized, ~12% unit-price rise, size elasticity ~0 for downsized) come from RePEc excerpt + secondary summary (koji.so); on screen use only the RePEc-confirmed 1.92% or no number from it. Never claim 'nobody noticed' as fact: say 'sales data barely moved'.
lenses.audience_psychology: Everyone has felt it (chips bag of air, smaller chocolate). Instant self-recognition plus a twist: the betrayal is about being fooled, not about money. Strong for Persian audience living with inflation and for international audience; business owners face the same decision now.
lenses.brand_fit: Pricing/communication strategy, directly actionable for owners: if you must cut, say it. Fits Behnood's strategist voice; not a repeat of Oct 23 (usage moment) or Oct 24 (distinctive assets).

candidates.title: Shrinkflation and Consumer Demand (scanner data, ~a decade, US)
candidates.claim: About 1.92% of products were downsized; downsizing usually without price cut, so unit prices rise; shoppers respond more to price than to size, so downsizing is an effective margin tool (abstract). Secondary summary: size elasticity ~0 for downsized products.
candidates.note: Merged into topic as the 'it works in the data' side of the tension.

candidates.title: Toblerone 2016: wider gaps between peaks, same box; 400g->360g, 170g->150g; Mondelez cites ingredient costs; 150g bar discontinued 2018
candidates.claim: UK bars shrank with packaging unchanged and gaps widened; public mockery; Mondelez: choice was shape change or price rise. 2018: '150g Toblerone is no longer being manufactured', 'only ever a short term response to cost increases' (ConfectioneryNews).
candidates.note: Concrete image for the hook. Do not show the brand logo as AI object; real photo only via owner upload, framed and credited. Do not claim the revert was caused by backlash (company gave cost/manufacturing reasons).

candidates.title: Austria's Anti-Deceptive Packaging Act: 60-day 'less content, higher price' notice when unit price rises >=3% with unchanged pack
candidates.claim: Retailers must label for 60 days; example wording 'Attention: Less content – higher price'; manufacturers must inform retailers; France, Romania, Hungary have similar rules (Yahoo/AFP).
candidates.note: Regulatory spark: governments now force the disclosure brands avoided. Mention as 'some countries now require a label' (no country name needed on screen).

candidates.title: Apple Music rebrand 'made by sound': note icon shaped by filmed vibrations in mineral oil (Fred again.., NEST Acoustics, TBWA\Media Arts Lab); red dropped for black/white
candidates.claim: Identity physically shaped by an original composition, captured in camera; ships with iOS 27.2. Beta tests showed red replaced by black/white; negative reaction on X (Cybernews, 2026-10-14).
candidates.note: Strongest news item, but central lesson (dropping a 13-year red) repeats yesterday's distinctive-assets topic; 'made by sound' angle is craft, low commercial utility for SME owners. Keep as a future topic (e.g. 'build the identity from what you sell').
